tags.gist: Calls silent upstream updates to hosted models a critical hurdle, to be met by local model locking, quality-system version management and automated drift detection.
Suggests deploying domain-specific small language models locally or in locked private environments, so weight updates come only through manufacturer release cycles.
Says locking shifts the burden to multi-version lifecycle management; FDA should encourage compatibility test matrices, revalidation suites and deprecation schedules in the QMS.
For unavoidable hosted APIs, wants automated golden benchmark runs, embedding-based drift analysis and guardrail trigger telemetry to catch behavior shifts.
Asks FDA to recognize local version locking as acceptable change-control mitigation, set standards for continuous automated benchmarking, and define multi-version documentation.
